subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB456. The receiver screen ('Identifier-3 shall be any item of class object that is permitted as a receiving item', with EXCEPTION-OBJECT refused per 8.4.3.6 SR1) was always complete and self-citing; the verdict rested on the statement never REACHING it. Format 5 used to be entered only when the sender was exactly one bare dataReference (OoExtractBareReference), so a literal or expression sender declined the re-route and dropped an object-reference receiver onto the Format-1 arithmetic path where no SET operand rule applied at all. Format 5 is now selected from the RECEIVING list, so every statement with an object-reference receiver reaches this screen whatever the sender looks like. WAVE-41 FINISHER: two more arms of the same rule. (a) The SENDER can now identify Format 5 where the receiving list could not: Format 1's identifier-1 brace admits any identifier, so SET N4 TO U selected Format 1 and the object sender reached the ARITHMETIC screen (COBOL0844, "'U' ... is not a numeric operand") while the rule the program broke was SR8. 8.8.1.1 admits only numeric operands in arithmetic-expression-1 and SR2 makes identifier-2 class index, so an item of class object is admissible in NO Format-1 sending position and is named by exactly one format's sending brace - SelectForTo picks it and SR8 refuses the receiver by name. (b) The receiver screen was ONE arm testing Resolve-or-category, so it stacked SR8 on top of the resolver's own COBOL1639 for an undefined name, and reported a FALSE 'not defined' for an INDEX-NAME receiver, which 13.18.38.3 SR7 permits in a SET statement and which is not a data reference at all; it is now three arms, one rule each. MEASURED at 2002/2014/2023: SET N4 TO U and SET IX TO U each draw exactly one COBOL0867.
